A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StochSync work and contain complete appendices A–G. Their text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original panorama-generation and mesh-texturing results, component ablations, inpainting experiments and a user preference study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds panorama examples and runtime measurements comparing two accelerator platforms.

M1.justification: Maximum stochasticity, multi-step clean-sample prediction, non-overlapping views, early stopping and DPM-Solver variants are retained. Algorithms 2 and 4 edit redundant input declarations and line numbering without changing the computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the PanFusion, L-MAGIC and horizon prompt sets, 429 mesh/prompt pairs, inpainting tests, 8K panoramas and Gaussian texturing. The added hardware experiment uses the existing panorama-generation task without establishing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The panorama, mesh-texturing and ablation comparator sets are retained. Appendix E separates quality and runtime summaries, with duplicated baseline quality results remaining in the main comparisons. The added Gaudi/A6000 comparison concerns hardware configurations.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a timing experiment comparing NVIDIA RTX A6000 and Intel Gaudi-v2 at 10, 30 and 50 iterations for multi-step clean-sample prediction (Figure 12). Existing benchmark metrics, sample sizes, user-study procedures and sampling schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a limited efficiency analysis examining runtime scaling across accelerator platforms and three prediction budgets, accompanied by Gaudi-generated examples (Figures 11–12). Existing component ablations, inpainting convergence tests and stochasticity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests for the reported comparisons; the added timing chart also has no error bars or repetition counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds three Gaudi panorama examples and accelerator timing results (Figures 11–12), with Gaudi slower at each plotted budget. Existing benchmark scores, user preferences and efficiency-variant scores and runtimes remain unchanged after matching the reorganized tables.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1 corrects the sampling formula for x_(t-Delta t), replacing alpha_t with alpha_(t-Delta t) in both signal and noise coefficients. The SDS-loss derivation, assumptions and informal SDE proof otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of connecting diffusion synchronization with SDS, improving depth-free panorama generation and achieving competitive depth-conditioned mesh texturing. No core contribution or application-scope claim changes.

C2.justification: Appendix E replaces acceleration 'without compromising quality' with acceleration involving 'a small amount of quality loss,' qualifying the interpretation of unchanged scores. The main mechanism explanations and limitations concerning NeRF/Gaussian generation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly identifies Intel Gaudi-v2 and NVIDIA RTX A6000 for the hardware experiment and gives its three prediction budgets. Existing implementation hyperparameters and the promise to release code remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and research positioning are unchanged. Bibliographic capitalization fixes and added mesh-figure attributions refer to works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, corrects algorithm references, clarifies the reproducibility statement, revises the efficiency discussion and adds acknowledgements. The overall narrative and section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v1 Tables 4–5 become separate quality Tables 4–5 and runtime Tables 6–7. v2 adds Figures 11–12, moves Tables 1–2 earlier, renumbers subsequent displays and adds citations to mesh-gallery labels. These are localized presentation changes.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects timestep indexing and better aligns the acceleration discussion with the retained scores by acknowledging quality loss. The added accelerator comparison provides limited practical evidence. These improve accuracy and usefulness while leaving the central method and main empirical validation unchanged.
